title: This Air Fryer Can Cook a Steak to Medium Rare—and Is Now Half Off
gist: An affiliate-linked deal post on Dreo's three-day flash sale (August 1–3): the probe-and-steam Chefmaker combi air fryer at 50 percent off and the TurboCool 765S misting fan at 30 percent off. The one non-obvious signal is that the reviewer reads the steep discount as inventory clearance ahead of a cheaper second-generation Chefmaker whose headline AI-recipe feature is expected to reach the current model by firmware anyway.

insights.claim: Dreo is running a three-day flash sale from August 1 to 3 with the Chefmaker combi air fryer at $180, half its $359 list price, versus $280 (22 percent off) on Amazon.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: A direct-channel price 36 percent below the Amazon promo shows Dreo pushing owned-channel sales, where it keeps marketplace margin.
insights.quote: This is the lowest price I’ve ever seen for this device, and the lowest price I expect to see.
insights.locator: Anyway, it’s half-price right now for three days only

insights.claim: The reviewer reads the 50 percent discount as clearance ahead of a second-generation Chefmaker that will be cheaper but ship with a downgraded screen — a deliberate move down-market rather than a product upgrade.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: Cost-down successors with reduced hardware are the standard playbook once a smart-appliance category shifts from early adopters to volume; expect margin per unit to compress.
insights.quote: The Chefmaker’s low price almost certainly presages the long-promised launch of Dreo’s second-generation Chefmaker—which will be a lower-cost device with a way less-cool screen.

insights.claim: The second-generation Chefmaker's main upgrade is AI recipes, but Dreo has signaled that AI-guided recipes will also reach the first-generation device as a firmware update.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: When the differentiating feature of a new hardware generation is software that back-ports to the old one, the hardware refresh loses its upgrade case — a recurring problem for connected-appliance vendors.
insights.quote: But Dreo has hinted that AI-guided recipes will be available as a firmware update for the Chefmaker 1 also.
insights.locator: The big upgrade on the soon-to-be-released device is access to AI recipes

themes.theme: What the Chefmaker actually does differently

insights.claim: The Chefmaker differentiates from basket air fryers by combining a built-in temperature probe with steam cooking, bringing meat slowly to target temperature before a final high-heat browning step.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: Probe-plus-steam is the feature set that lets a sub-$400 countertop device attack sous-vide and oven use cases, expanding the addressable job beyond fried snacks.
insights.quote: It’s got a built-in probe and steam cooking—so it can bring any meat up slowly to the desired temperature
insights.locator: That’s because it doesn’t work like other air fryers

insights.claim: Temperature accuracy is only reliable in probe-assisted mode; the classic non-probe air fry and toaster oven modes can drift roughly 20 degrees off the set point.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: The precision claim only holds for one cooking path — a caveat that undercuts the premium positioning for buyers using it as a general oven.
insights.quote: the thermostat on the “classic” nonprobe air fry or toaster oven cooks can swing off target by 20 degrees or so
insights.locator: Just note that while the probe-assisted cook is very well regulated

themes.theme: Misting fan and cross-product tech reuse

insights.claim: Dreo's TurboCool 765S misting tower fan is $140 in the sale, 30 percent off its $200 list, versus only 10 percent off on Amazon.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: The same direct-versus-Amazon discount spread appears across Dreo's line, confirming a channel strategy rather than a one-product clearance.
insights.quote: For only three days, the fan is available for $140, 30 percent off its usual price of $200.
insights.locator: Also: 30 Percent Off on Dreo’s Misting Fan

insights.claim: The 12-speed TurboCool 765S borrows technology from Dreo's humidifier line to diffuse ultrafine mist particles of about 17 microns, solving the wetness problem that makes most misting fans unusable — a tester stood in front of it at maximum mist and stayed dry.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: Component reuse across appliance categories is how small hardware brands buy differentiation cheaply; look for the same pattern in adjacent Dreo launches.
insights.quote: Merck stood right in front of this fan at its highest mist setting, and her clothes and skin remained dry after several minutes.
insights.locator: But the 12-speed TurboCool 765S misting tower fan

insights.claim: The article carries an explicit affiliate disclosure that the publisher may be compensated by retailers and by purchases made through its links, which is the correct discount to apply to its enthusiasm.
insights.speaker: Matthew Korfhage
insights.so_what: Deal coverage of this kind is a monetization product, not independent demand evidence — do not read it as a signal about Dreo sell-through.
insights.quote: we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links
insights.locator: All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors
